currentGoalSemanticSnapshot.title: Reaktionsenthalpien aus Bindungsverhältnissen begründen
currentGoalSemanticSnapshot.titleEn: Justify reaction enthalpies from bonding relationships
currentGoalSemanticSnapshot.description: Die lernende Person kann Unterschiede experimentell bestimmter oder vorgegebener Reaktionsenthalpien auf Grundlage der Bindungsverhältnisse begründen und die verglichenen Edukt- und Produktsysteme relativ zueinander als energiereich oder energiearm einstufen.
currentGoalSemanticSnapshot.descriptionEn: The learner can justify differences in experimentally determined or given reaction enthalpies based on bonding relationships and classify the compared reactant and product systems as energy-rich or energy-poor relative to one another.

scientificFindings: Bond breaking requires energy; forming bonds releases energy. The hammer is a mechanism metaphor, not a laboratory procedure or a claim atoms are destroyed.

The exothermic example has reactants above products and outward energy arrows; the endothermic example has products above reactants and incoming energy. Relative H positions and qualitative energy-budget statements agree.

The panels are two independently labelled qualitative reaction classes, with anonymous jars/canisters. There is no element legend, named reactant/product identity, stoichiometric formula or claim one specific reaction has both signs.
The visibly prominent footer Gas-Modell: Näherung limits the bond-energy model; the generic containers are system placeholders, not a measured liquid/gas state or thermodynamic material database.
Coins have no numerical unit or counting legend: their drawn count is not a quantitative energy budget. No reaction enthalpy calculation or universal phase-independence is proved.
imageOnlyQualificationsAlreadyVisible: Exotherm / Endotherm as separate qualitative classes
Correct relative reactant/product height and direction of exchange
assets.requiredNewVisibleQualification: None for this actual candidate; preserve its existing gas-model footer and distinct class headings on adoption.

readability.native: All labels, arrows, bond metaphor and relative levels inspectable.
readability.phone360: Title, breaking/forming labels, exo/endo headings, broad energy arrows, heights and gas-model footer remain clear. Fine H/Enthalpie/energy-content annotations are small; they are supplementary, not the sole source of the distinction.
readability.desktop680: Important labels and relative heights are readily readable; remains within448px height cap.
readability.style: Friendly rounded blue/red comic panels, large hammer/coin metaphors and abstract system vessels fit the requested landscape. PNG1672x941 is close native16:9.

assets.provenance: Upstream generation receipt declares OpenAI built-in image_gen; exact model is not exposed. This lane inspected metadata fields only, not upstream visual verdicts.
assets.recommendedAltDe: Comic-Schema zu Bindungen und Energie: Das Lösen einer Bindung benötigt Energie, ihre Bildung setzt Energie frei. Zwei getrennte qualitative Modellfälle zeigen Edukte über Produkten bei einer exothermen Reaktion mit Energieabgabe und Produkte über Edukten bei einer endothermen Reaktion mit Energieaufnahme. Die Gefäße stehen für unbenannte Systeme, die Münzen symbolisieren Energie ohne Zahlenmaßstab. Sichtbar gekennzeichnet: Gas-Modell, Näherung.
noClaim: No fixed magnitudes from coin counts
No measured enthalpy or phase-correction data

currentGoalSemanticSnapshot.title: Erdölprodukte in Alltag, Technik und Umwelt bewerten
currentGoalSemanticSnapshot.titleEn: Evaluate petroleum products in everyday life, technology, and the environment
currentGoalSemanticSnapshot.description: Die lernende Person kann wichtige Erdölprodukte ihren Einsatzbereichen in Alltag und Technik zuordnen und Nutzen sowie ökologische Konsequenzen ihres Einsatzes begründet bewerten.
currentGoalSemanticSnapshot.descriptionEn: The learner can assign important petroleum products to their applications in everyday life and technology and give a reasoned assessment of the benefits and ecological consequences of their use.

scientificFindings: Refinery plus processing routes petroleum inputs to fuels, plastics, heating oil, pharmaceutical/cosmetic feedstocks, lubricants, bitumen/asphalt road use, basic chemicals and synthetic-rubber tyres. Processing is visible; the drawing does not claim all products emerge unchanged from crude oil.

Asphalt(Bitumen) is a use/binder association in this overview, not a reviewed identity statement that bitumen and the full aggregate asphalt mixture are chemically identical. Alt should name bitumen for road asphalt.

Burning/CO2/climate, persistent plastic litter and fragmentation, oil spills during transport/production and finite nonrenewable resources are valid broad environmental issue classes. Bottles are macro-litter examples beside a microplastic issue heading, not a claim those bottles themselves have microscopic size.
The central scale and check icon denote reasoned evaluation; there is no numeric life-cycle verdict or claim petroleum products are universally environmentally harmless.
The picture supports orientation in the revised assignment+benefit/ecological-assessment goal; it supplies no complete comparison of benefits, alternatives or life-cycle evidence.
imageOnlyQualificationsAlreadyVisible: Usage and environmental consequence categories, with no ranking or numerical weights
assets.requiredNewVisibleQualification: None; this is a valid bounded overview. Do not reuse it as a completed environmental assessment or all-product provenance proof.

readability.native: Full category labels and examples inspectable.
readability.phone360: Oil barrel/refinery branching, car/fuel, bottle/toy, heater, oiling machinery, road roller and tyre icons remain identifiable; the lower climate/litter/oil-spill/resource scenes also remain identifiable. Many secondary labels are too small for comfortable reading, so the image is used as a visual overview with accessible alt, not a read-required eight-category table.
readability.desktop680: Main category labels and causal headings readable; fine examples still smaller than body text. No height cap truncation.
readability.style: Friendly coloured panels and thick-outline everyday icons remain compatible with the existing landscape. Good existing JPEG2752x1536 retained regardless of format/provider.

assets.provenance: Current canonical resource metadata declares Google Gemini / Nano Banana Pro; no new generation or upstream API provenance audit in this lane.
assets.recommendedAltDe: Übersicht: Erdöl wird in einer Raffinerie und weiteren Verarbeitungsschritten für Kraftstoffe, Kunststoffe, Heizöl, pharmazeutische und kosmetische Grundstoffe, Schmierstoffe, Bitumen für Straßenasphalt, Grundchemikalien und synthetischen Reifenkautschuk genutzt. Darunter stehen Beispiele möglicher Folgen: CO2 aus Verbrennung, langlebiger Plastikmüll und Mikroplastik, Ölunfälle sowie Verbrauch endlicher Ressourcen. Die Waage steht für begründete Bewertung; das Bild enthält keine vollständige Ökobilanz.

No literal macro-bottle equals microplastic claim

currentGoalSemanticSnapshot.title: Innere Energie und Enthalpie in Reaktionssystemen abgrenzen
currentGoalSemanticSnapshot.titleEn: Distinguish internal energy and enthalpy in reaction systems
currentGoalSemanticSnapshot.description: Die lernende Person kann unterschiedliche Reaktionssysteme unterscheiden, Wärme und Arbeit als Formen der Energieänderung in einem geschlossenen System mit variablem Volumen beschreiben und die Änderung der inneren Energie (Reaktionsenergie) von der Änderung der Enthalpie (Reaktionsenthalpie) abgrenzen.
currentGoalSemanticSnapshot.descriptionEn: The learner can distinguish different reaction systems, describe heat and work as forms of energy change in a closed system with variable volume, and distinguish the change in internal energy (reaction energy) from the change in enthalpy (reaction enthalpy).

scientificFindings: The visibly stated closed-system/constant-volume flask and closed-system/constant-pressure piston are a standard bounded heat-and-volume-work comparison. Heat enters both; only the piston example shows outward volume work. Closed is not presented as isolated.

W is visibly qualified as Volumenänderung on the work arrow and keine Volumenarbeit under the rigid-vessel case. The depicted work channel is volume work, not an unrestricted catalogue of all possible work forms.

For the illustrated closed only-pV-work model: at fixed V, Wv=0 and Qv=deltaU; at constant mechanically balanced pressure, Wv=-p deltaV and Qp=deltaH; deltaH=deltaU+p deltaV at constant p. Expansion energy leaves the system, consistent with the chemistry work sign.
The parenthetic Innere Energie/Enthalpie names the quantities associated with their explicitly visible delta symbols; the formula is not Q=U or Q=H.

The dot-and-stick particles have no element legend or reaction identity. They are qualitative contents, not a reviewed stoichiometric reaction; no molecular valence conclusion is claimed from arbitrary colours.
imageOnlyQualificationsAlreadyVisible: Delta symbols in the heat/energy relations
assets.requiredNewVisibleQualification: None for the actually drawn only-volume-work model. Bounded KEEP does not universalise these equalities to an electrical/shaft-work system that is absent from the image. Alt must describe this visible work-channel scope explicitly.

readability.native: All labels, delta symbols, volume-work sign and system boundaries inspected.
readability.phone360: Sealed flask versus piston, heat-in arrows, work-out arrow and the two principal Q=delta relations remain recognizable; fine explanatory/system labels and subscripts are small. The image is orientation, not a phone-readable equation reference sheet.
readability.desktop680: Principal labels and formulas readable; preserved full composition within448px cap.
readability.style: Abstract thick-outline apparatus and a soft grid fit a schematic chemistry image; more technical than the new comic, but no concrete quality failure justifies replacing this existing asset.

assets.provenance: Current canonical resource metadata declares Google Gemini / Nano Banana Pro (gemini-3-pro-image); this lane makes no fresh provider/API claim.
assets.recommendedAltDe: Zwei geschlossene Modelle mit Wärmeaustausch und ausschließlich Volumenarbeit: Links bleibt das Volumen im starren Gefäß konstant, es gibt keine Volumenarbeit und die aufgenommene Wärme ist Qv=ΔU. Rechts zeigt ein beweglicher Kolben konstanten, mechanisch ausgeglichenen Druck; bei Expansion gibt das System Volumenarbeit ab, W=−pΔV. Für dieses Modell gilt Qp=ΔH und ΔH=ΔU+pΔV. Die Änderungssymbole beziehen sich auf Energieänderungen; das Bild behandelt keine zusätzlichen Arbeitsformen.
noClaim: No universal rigid-vessel no-total-work assertion with extra electrical/shaft work
No microscopic species or reaction-balance statement
No total U/H equals heat statement

selectedSourceGoalsActuallyRead.sourceText: beurteilen die Bedeutung von Erdölprodukten in verschiedenen Einsatzbereichen in Alltag und Technik und schätzen die Konsequenzen des Einsatzes für die Umwelt ab.

unterscheiden verschiedene Systeme, in denen chemische Reaktionen ablaufen, und beschreiben, dass die bei einer chemischen Reaktion im geschlossenen System (bei variablem Volumen) auftretende Energieänderung in Form von Wärme und Arbeit auftreten kann, um die Änderung der inneren Energie (Reaktionsenergie) von der Änderung der Enthalpie (Reaktionsenthalpie) abzugrenzen.
begründen die Unterschiede von experimentell bestimmten oder vorgegebenen Reaktionsenthalpien auf der Grundlage der Bindungsverhältnisse und stufen Systeme als energiereich oder energiearm ein.
